g.textArea: Execution policy: explicit final-plan approval for staging/production is proposed; dev approval policy remains a team decision.
Failure rule: failed or changed final plan blocks apply; regenerate and renew authorization. PR updates rerun checks and review.
Target comes from the selected root, inputs and backend/state. Each environment has its own plan; promotion does not reuse a dev plan.

GitHub Actions runner executes commands; the target is the cloud infrastructure selected by the Terraform root.

Decide what gets checked, who approves
each environment, and how we keep
the code and final plan in sync.

rect.data-content:
3. Try it in development
Build the agreed workflow for a small
development scope. Check that review,
approval, apply and reporting work.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: DevOps
Evidence required before the pilot is ready

rect.data-content:
• See the changes: PR checks show a plan for every affected infrastructure component (Terraform root).
• Review current code: code changes after approval require a new review.
• Check the final plan: it must match the exact code version, target settings and current state.
• Control execution: only authorized execution can apply; record the outcome and any failures.

Team decisions
• Decide who approves execution for dev, staging and production.
• Choose the approval mechanism and execution identities.
• Agree pilot components, owners and completion criteria.

g.textArea: Dependencies: approved planner/apply identities, state access and concurrency control; no monorepo migration prerequisite.
Legend: blue = proposed | gray = context / acceptance evidence | yellow = decision or exception
No implementation approval, rollout dates or named owners are implied. GitHub protected approval support must be checked for the repository plan.
Environment targeting and coverage

rect.data-content:
• Separate targets: plan each environment using its own settings and state (Terraform’s record of managed resources).
• Shared code: when reusable configuration (a module) changes, check every component that uses it.
• Agree coverage: explicitly list shared/common services, RD and protected foundations in scope.
• Keep QA/lab provisioning in its separate proposal.

Plan freshness
• Another merge or cloud change can alter the final plan.
• Re-plan and approve again when a plan is stale.
• Run one apply at a time for the same state.

g.textArea: Scope: decide which infrastructure the workflow covers; each environment needs its own plan.
Before the pilot: prove the change is visible, reviewed, applied to the right target, and traceable.
